instance_description:
Setting: A 2026 personal consumer-finance workspace for a liveaboard recreational sailboat resident moored in Tacoma, Washington, managing ordinary costs outside business use.
Scope: Recurring activities include marina fees, shore power, fuel, insurance paperwork, vessel maintenance purchases, storage, mail forwarding, safety gear, subscriptions, refunds, and warranty documentation.
Resources: Household records include account and equipment references, standing preferences, service contacts, personal receipts, calendars, and reusable workpads.
Exclusions: No investment trading, business bookkeeping, tax filing advice, legal strategy, marine licensing compliance advice, lending applications, or irreversible high-stakes financial commitments.
personal_description:
Identity: Talia Mireven Cross is a 37-year-old museum exhibit fabricator who lives aboard her privately owned 30-foot sailboat and manages her own consumer records.
Responsibilities: She tracks routine liveaboard expenses, keeps marina and service documentation, compares personal vendors, stores receipts, follows refund issues, and prepares insurance or warranty information.
Authority: Talia can organize records, draft merchant or insurer messages, categorize expenses, prepare payment checklists, and document consumer follow-ups for her own personal life.
Restrictions: She cannot manage marina accounts, run charter finances, provide professional advice, bypass account security, trade securities, or authorize actual payments without explicit owner authorization.
